<!-- generated by tools/gen-config.py from data/config/*.json (or the Director's .grammar). Do not edit by hand. -->

A JobDefs resource holds defaults for Job resources: a Job with JobDefs = name takes every directive it does not set itself from it. It accepts the same directives as a Job; none is required in a JobDefs.

## Examples

**Defaults shared by the backup jobs**

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Type = Backup
  Level = Incremental
  FileSet = LinuxAll
  Schedule = WeeklyCycle
  Storage = File
  Messages = Standard
  Pool = Incremental
  Priority = 10
  Write Bootstrap = "/var/lib/bareos/%c.bsr"
  Full Backup Pool = Full
  Differential Backup Pool = Differential
  Incremental Backup Pool = Incremental
}
```

| [Prefer Mounted Volumes](#d-prefermountedvolumes) | yes\|no | `yes` |  | Prefer a drive that has a usable volume mounted. |

| [Allow Mixed Priority](#d-allowmixedpriority) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Allow this job to run together with jobs of other priorities, as long as they allow it as well. |

| [Accurate](#d-accurate) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Accurate mode: the File Daemon receives the file list of the previous backups and also records deleted and renamed files, so a restore gives exactly the state of the backup. |
| [Allow Duplicate Jobs](#d-allowduplicatejobs) | yes\|no | `yes` |  | Allow a second run of the same job while one is queued or running. |
| [Allow Higher Duplicates](#d-allowhigherduplicates) | yes\|no | `yes` | deprecated | Deprecated: allow duplicates of a higher level. |
| [Cancel Lower Level Duplicates](#d-cancellowerlevelduplicates) | yes\|no | `no` |  | With Allow Duplicate Jobs = no: cancel the duplicate of the lower level (an Incremental gives way to a Full). |
| [Cancel Queued Duplicates](#d-cancelqueuedduplicates) | yes\|no | `no` |  | With Allow Duplicate Jobs = no: cancel a duplicate that is still waiting in the queue. |
| [Cancel Running Duplicates](#d-cancelrunningduplicates) | yes\|no | `no` |  | With Allow Duplicate Jobs = no: cancel the duplicate that is already running in favour of the new one. |
| [Save File History](#d-savefilehistory) | yes\|no | `yes` |  | For NDMP: store the file history sent by the filer, so single files can be restored. |
| [File History Size](#d-filehistorysize) | size | `10000000` |  | For NDMP: size of the file history buffer. |
| [FD Plugin Options](#d-fdpluginoptions) | string list |  |  | Options passed to the File Daemon plugins of this job. |
| [SD Plugin Options](#d-sdpluginoptions) | string list |  |  | Options passed to the Storage Daemon plugins of this job. |
| [Dir Plugin Options](#d-dirpluginoptions) | string list |  |  | Options passed to the Director plugins of this job. |
| [Max Concurrent Copies](#d-maxconcurrentcopies) | positive integer | `100` |  | For Copy jobs: how many copy jobs are started at once from one selection. |
| [Always Incremental](#d-alwaysincremental) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Always Incremental scheme: only Incrementals are taken, and a Consolidate job merges the old ones into a VirtualFull. |
| [Always Incremental Job Retention](#d-alwaysincrementaljobretention) | time | `0` |  | Incrementals younger than this are not consolidated. |
| [Always Incremental Keep Number](#d-alwaysincrementalkeepnumber) | positive integer | `0` |  | How many Incrementals are always kept unconsolidated, even when they are older than the retention. |
| [Always Incremental Max Full Age](#d-alwaysincrementalmaxfullage) | time |  |  | When the Full of an Always Incremental chain is older than this, the Consolidate job includes it, so the Full does not grow old. |
| [Max Full Consolidations](#d-maxfullconsolidations) | positive integer | `0` |  | How many Fulls a Consolidate job may consolidate in one run (because of Always Incremental Max Full Age); 0 means no limit. |
| [Run On Incoming Connect Interval](#d-runonincomingconnectinterval) | time | `0` |  | For clients that connect to the Director (Connection From Client To Director): start this job when the client connects and the last run is older than this interval. 0 switches it off. |

### Name {#d-name}

Key: `name` · Type: name

Name of the job. It appears in job lists, logs and the catalog; renaming it starts a new history, so the next Incremental becomes a Full.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = "backup-web"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure add jobdefs name=DefaultJob type=Backup messages=Standard pool=Incremental
```

### Description {#d-description}

Key: `description` · Type: string

Free text describing the job.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Description = "Nightly backup of the web server"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob description="Nightly backup of the web server"
```

### Type {#d-type}

Key: `type` · Type: enum · Values: `Backup`, `Restore`, `Verify`, `Admin`, `Archive`, `Migrate`, `Copy`, `Consolidate`

What the job does: Backup, Restore, Verify, Admin (runs only its scripts), Migrate, Copy, Consolidate (Always Incremental), or Archive. Required, directly or through JobDefs.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Type = Backup
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob type=Backup
```

Key: `protocol` · Type: enum · Default: `Native` · Values: `Native`, `NDMP_BAREOS`, `NDMP_NATIVE`

Backup protocol: Native for the Bareos File Daemon; NDMP\_BAREOS or NDMP\_NATIVE for NAS filers (data stored by Bareos or by an NDMP tape server).

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Protocol = Native
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob protocol=Native
```

Key: `backupformat` · Type: string · Default: `Native`

Format of NDMP backups (for example dump or tar, depending on the filer); Native for normal jobs.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Backup Format = Native
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob backupformat=Native
```

### Level {#d-level}

Key: `level` · Type: enum · Values: `Full`, `Incremental`, `Differential`, `VirtualFull`, `Base`, `Since`, `InitCatalog`, `Catalog`, `VolumeToCatalog`, `DiskToCatalog`, `Data`

Default level of the job: for backups Full, Incremental, Differential or VirtualFull; for verify jobs InitCatalog, Catalog, VolumeToCatalog, DiskToCatalog or Data. A Run line of the Schedule or run level= overrides it. An Incremental or Differential without a Full before it is upgraded to Full.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Level = Incremental
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob level=Incremental
```

### Messages {#d-messages}

Key: `messages` · Type: resource

Messages resource that decides where the job's messages go (job log in the catalog, mail, log file). Required.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Messages = "Standard"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob messages=Standard
```

### Storage {#d-storage}

Key: `storage` · Type: resource list

Storage the job writes to (or reads from). Several may be listed; the first available one is used. A Storage in the Pool takes precedence over the job's.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Storage = "File"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob storage=File
```

### Pool {#d-pool}

Key: `pool` · Type: resource

Pool the job writes to. Required for backups; Full Backup Pool and the other level pools and Run line overrides can choose another one per level.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Pool = "Incremental"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob pool=Incremental
```

### Client {#d-client}

Key: `client` · Type: resource

Client (File Daemon) the job backs up or, for restores, restores to by default. Required for backups.

Key: `fileset` · Type: resource

FileSet that says what is backed up. Changing the FileSet makes the next Incremental or Differential a Full unless Ignore FileSet Changes is set.

Key: `schedule` · Type: resource

Schedule that starts the job automatically. Without it, the job only runs when it is started by hand or by another job.


Key: `jobtoverify` · Type: resource · Aliases: Verify Job

For verify jobs: the backup job whose last run is verified (levels Catalog, VolumeToCatalog, Data).

Key: `catalog` · Type: resource

### Job Defs {#d-jobdefs}

Key: `jobdefs` · Type: resource

JobDefs resource whose directives this job inherits. Directives written in the job itself win. The Onesimus GUI shows which values come from the JobDefs.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Job Defs = "DefaultJob"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob jobdefs=DefaultJob
```

### Run {#d-run}

Key: `run` · Type: string list

Starts another job (or a copy of this one with other settings) when this job is started, in run command syntax, for example a second backup to another storage. It is rarely needed; Copy jobs are the usual way to a second copy.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Run = "backup-web-copy level=%l since=\"%s\""
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob run="backup-web-copy level=%l since=\"%s\""
```

### Where {#d-where}

Key: `where` · Type: path

For restore jobs: directory prefix the files are restored under. / restores to the original place. The restore command and the GUI can change it per restore, within the console's Where ACL.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Where = "/tmp/bareos-restores"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob where=/tmp/bareos-restores
```

Key: `regexwhere` · Type: string

For restore jobs: rewrites the paths of restored files with sed-like expressions (!from!to!), instead of a plain prefix.

```text

  Regex Where = "!/home!/srv/restored-home!"
}
```

In the console:

### Bootstrap {#d-bootstrap}

Key: `bootstrap` · Type: path

Bootstrap file a restore job reads to find the data on the volumes. Usually written by the restore command itself.

```text
}
```

In the console:

### Write Bootstrap {#d-writebootstrap}

Key: `writebootstrap` · Type: path or |command

File (or, starting with |, a command) the job writes its bootstrap to after a backup: which volumes and blocks hold this job. With it a restore is possible even without the catalog, so keep it off the backup server. %c, %n and other job variables are replaced.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Write Bootstrap = "/var/lib/bareos/%c.bsr"
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob writebootstrap=/var/lib/bareos/%c.bsr
```

Key: `writeverifylist` · Type: path · Deprecated

Deprecated: file the verify job writes its list of files to.

```text

  Name = DefaultJob
  Write Verify List = "/var/lib/bareos/verify.lst"
}
```

### Replace {#d-replace}

Key: `replace` · Type: enum · Default: `Always` · Values: `always`, `ifnewer`, `ifolder`, `never`

For restore jobs: what happens to files that exist already: always (overwrite), ifnewer (only if the backup is newer), ifolder (only if it is older) or never.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Replace = IfNewer
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob replace=IfNewer
```

### Maximum Bandwidth {#d-maximumbandwidth}

Key: `maximumbandwidth` · Type: speed

Limits the bandwidth of this job. Speeds take the suffixes k/s, m/s (powers of 1024) or kb/s, mb/s (powers of 1000); a plain number means bytes per second.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Maximum Bandwidth = 10 m/s
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob maximumbandwidth="10 m/s"
```

### Max Run Sched Time {#d-maxrunschedtime}

Key: `maxrunschedtime` · Type: time

Cancels the job if it has not finished this long after its scheduled time (waiting counts). Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Max Run Sched Time = 10 hours
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob maxrunschedtime="10 hours"
```

### Max Run Time {#d-maxruntime}

Key: `maxruntime` · Type: time

Cancels the job if it runs longer than this from its actual start. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Max Run Time = 8 hours
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob maxruntime="8 hours"
```

### Full Max Runtime {#d-fullmaxruntime}

Key: `fullmaxruntime` · Type: time

Max Run Time for Full runs only. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Full Max Runtime = 12 hours
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob fullmaxruntime="12 hours"
```

### Incremental Max Runtime {#d-incrementalmaxruntime}

Key: `incrementalmaxruntime` · Type: time

Max Run Time for Incremental runs only. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Incremental Max Runtime = 2 hours
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob incrementalmaxruntime="2 hours"
```

### Differential Max Runtime {#d-differentialmaxruntime}

Key: `differentialmaxruntime` · Type: time

Max Run Time for Differential runs only. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Differential Max Runtime = 4 hours
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob differentialmaxruntime="4 hours"
```

### Max Wait Time {#d-maxwaittime}

Key: `maxwaittime` · Type: time

Cancels the job if it waits longer than this for a resource (a volume, a device, a concurrency slot) after it started. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Max Wait Time = 1 hour
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob maxwaittime="1 hour"
```

### Max Start Delay {#d-maxstartdelay}

Key: `maxstartdelay` · Type: time

Cancels the job if it cannot start within this time after its scheduled time, so a nightly job that missed its window does not run in the day. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Max Start Delay = 4 hours
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob maxstartdelay="4 hours"
```

### Max Full Interval {#d-maxfullinterval}

Key: `maxfullinterval` · Type: time

Upgrades an Incremental or Differential to Full when the last successful Full is older than this. A simple way to get regular Fulls without a Full Run line. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Max Full Interval = 30 days
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob maxfullinterval="30 days"
```

### Max Virtual Full Interval {#d-maxvirtualfullinterval}

Key: `maxvirtualfullinterval` · Type: time

Upgrades a run to VirtualFull when the last VirtualFull (or Full) is older than this. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Max Virtual Full Interval = 7 days
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob maxvirtualfullinterval="7 days"
```

### Max Diff Interval {#d-maxdiffinterval}

Key: `maxdiffinterval` · Type: time

Upgrades an Incremental to Differential when the last Differential is older than this. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Max Diff Interval = 7 days
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob maxdiffinterval="7 days"
```

Key: `prunevolumes` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Prune the volumes of the pool after the job.

Key: `purgemigrationjob` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

### Enabled {#d-enabled}

Key: `enabled` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

A disabled job is not started by its schedule; it can still be run by hand. enable job and disable job change it at run time.

```text

  Name = DefaultJob
  Enabled = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text

```

### Spool Attributes {#d-spoolattributes}

Key: `spoolattributes` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Spool the file attributes on the Storage Daemon and insert them into the catalog at the end of the job, instead of while writing. Speeds up jobs with many small files.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Spool Attributes = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text

```

### Spool Data {#d-spooldata}

Key: `spooldata` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Spool the data to disk on the Storage Daemon first and write it to the volume in big chunks. Meant for tape drives that would otherwise stop and start (shoe-shining). It implies Spool Attributes.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Spool Data = yes
}
```

```text

```

### Spool Size {#d-spoolsize}

Key: `spoolsize` · Type: size

Upper limit of the spool file of this job. Sizes take the suffixes k, m, g, t (powers of 1024) or kb, mb, gb, tb (powers of 1000).

```text

}
```

In the console:


### Rerun Failed Levels {#d-rerunfailedlevels}

Key: `rerunfailedlevels` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

If the last Full (or Differential) failed, run the next job at that level again instead of the scheduled lower level.

```text

  Name = DefaultJob

}
```

In the console:


Key: `prefermountedvolumes` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Prefer a drive that has a usable volume mounted. With no, the Director prefers an idle drive, which spreads jobs over several drives.

```text
}
```

Key: `clientrunbeforejob` · Type: command

Command the File Daemon runs on the client before the backup, for example a database dump. A failing command cancels the job.

```text
}
```

In the console:


### Client Run After Job {#d-clientrunafterjob}

Key: `clientrunafterjob` · Type: command

Command the File Daemon runs on the client after the job.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Client Run After Job = "/usr/local/bin/cleanup-dump"
}
```

In the console:

```text

```

### Maximum Concurrent Jobs {#d-maximumconcurrentjobs}

Key: `maximumconcurrentjobs` · Type: positive integer · Default: `1`

How many runs of this job may run at the same time; usually 1, so a slow run is not overtaken by the next one.

```text

  Name = DefaultJob
  Maximum Concurrent Jobs = 1
}
```

In the console:

```text

```

### Reschedule On Error {#d-rescheduleonerror}

Key: `rescheduleonerror` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Start the job again when it failed, after Reschedule Interval, at most Reschedule Times times.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Reschedule On Error = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob rescheduleonerror=yes
```

### Reschedule Interval {#d-rescheduleinterval}

Key: `rescheduleinterval` · Type: time · Default: `1800` (30 minutes)

Wait between a failed run and its retry. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Reschedule Interval = 30 minutes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob rescheduleinterval="30 minutes"
```

### Reschedule Times {#d-rescheduletimes}

Key: `rescheduletimes` · Type: positive integer · Default: `5`

How many times a failed job is retried; 0 means without limit.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Reschedule Times = 3
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob rescheduletimes=3
```

### Priority {#d-priority}

Key: `priority` · Type: positive integer · Default: `10`

Priority of the job: smaller numbers first. Jobs of different priorities do not run at the same time (unless Allow Mixed Priority): a job waits until all jobs of a higher priority are done. Use it for example to run the catalog backup after all others. The schedule view of the Onesimus GUI does not count such waits as avoidable.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Priority = 10
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob priority=10
```

### Allow Mixed Priority {#d-allowmixedpriority}

Key: `allowmixedpriority` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Allow this job to run together with jobs of other priorities, as long as they allow it as well.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Allow Mixed Priority = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob allowmixedpriority=yes
```

### Selection Pattern {#d-selectionpattern}

Key: `selectionpattern` · Type: string

For Copy and Migrate jobs: the pattern or SQL query used by Selection Type (a job or client name pattern, or a query returning job IDs).

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Selection Pattern = "backup-.*"
}
```

In the console:

```text

```

### Run Script {#d-runscript}

Key: `runscript` · Type: block

Block that runs a command or console command before or after the job, on the Director or the client, with control over failure handling. See the RunScript block.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Run Script {
    RunsWhen = Before
    RunsOnClient = yes
    FailJobOnError = yes
    Command = "/usr/local/bin/dump-database"
  }
}
```

### Selection Type {#d-selectiontype}

Key: `selectiontype` · Type: enum · Values: `SmallestVolume`, `OldestVolume`, `PoolOccupancy`, `PoolTime`, `PoolUncopiedJobs`, `Client`, `Volume`, `Job`, `SQLQuery`

For Copy and Migrate jobs: how the source jobs are chosen: SmallestVolume, OldestVolume, Client, Volume, Job, SQLQuery, PoolOccupancy, PoolTime, PoolUncopiedJobs.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Selection Type = PoolUncopiedJobs
}
```

In the console:

```text

```

### Accurate {#d-accurate}

Key: `accurate` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Accurate mode: the File Daemon receives the file list of the previous backups and also records deleted and renamed files, so a restore gives exactly the state of the backup. Needed for Always Incremental and VirtualFull; costs memory on the client.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Accurate = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob accurate=yes
```

Key: `allowduplicatejobs` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Allow a second run of the same job while one is queued or running. With no, the Cancel ... Duplicates directives decide which one is canceled.

Key: `allowhigherduplicates` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no` · Deprecated

```text
  Name = DefaultJob
  Cancel Queued Duplicates = yes

```

In the console:

### Cancel Running Duplicates {#d-cancelrunningduplicates}

Key: `cancelrunningduplicates` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

With Allow Duplicate Jobs = no: cancel the duplicate that is already running in favour of the new one.

### Always Incremental {#d-alwaysincremental}

Key: `alwaysincremental` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Always Incremental scheme: only Incrementals are taken, and a Consolidate job merges the old ones into a VirtualFull. Needs Accurate and pools for the consolidated data.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Always Incremental = yes
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob alwaysincremental=yes
```

### Always Incremental Job Retention {#d-alwaysincrementaljobretention}

Key: `alwaysincrementaljobretention` · Type: time · Default: `0`

Incrementals younger than this are not consolidated. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Always Incremental Job Retention = 7 days
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob alwaysincrementaljobretention="7 days"
```

### Always Incremental Keep Number {#d-alwaysincrementalkeepnumber}

Key: `alwaysincrementalkeepnumber` · Type: positive integer · Default: `0`

How many Incrementals are always kept unconsolidated, even when they are older than the retention.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Always Incremental Keep Number = 7
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob alwaysincrementalkeepnumber=7
```

### Always Incremental Max Full Age {#d-alwaysincrementalmaxfullage}

Key: `alwaysincrementalmaxfullage` · Type: time

When the Full of an Always Incremental chain is older than this, the Consolidate job includes it, so the Full does not grow old. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Always Incremental Max Full Age = 30 days
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob alwaysincrementalmaxfullage="30 days"
```

### Max Full Consolidations {#d-maxfullconsolidations}

Key: `maxfullconsolidations` · Type: positive integer · Default: `0`

How many Fulls a Consolidate job may consolidate in one run (because of Always Incremental Max Full Age); 0 means no limit. Only valid for Consolidate jobs.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Max Full Consolidations = 1
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob maxfullconsolidations=1
```

### Run On Incoming Connect Interval {#d-runonincomingconnectinterval}

Key: `runonincomingconnectinterval` · Type: time · Default: `0`

For clients that connect to the Director (Connection From Client To Director): start this job when the client connects and the last run is older than this interval. 0 switches it off. Times are written as a number with a unit: seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, quarters or years (abbreviations such as 30d, 12h or 1y work too); several parts add up ("1 month 15 days"), and a plain number means seconds.

```text
JobDefs {
  Name = DefaultJob
  Run On Incoming Connect Interval = 1 day
}
```

In the console:

```text
configure update jobdefs=DefaultJob runonincomingconnectinterval="1 day"
```

## RunScript block {#block-runscript}

Runs a command or console command before or after the job, on the Director or the client. Several RunScript blocks may be given.

| Directive | Type | Default | | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Command](#b-runscript-command) | string |  |  | Shell command to run; repeatable. |
| [Console](#b-runscript-console) | string |  |  | Console command the Director runs instead of a shell command, for example to start another job or update a volume. |
| [Runs When](#b-runscript-runswhen) | enum | `Never` |  | When the script runs: Before the job, After it, AfterVSS (Windows, after the snapshot), Always (before and after) or Queued (when the job enters the queue). |
| [Runs On Client](#b-runscript-runsonclient) | yes\|no | `yes` |  | Run the command on the client (by the File Daemon) instead of on the Director. |
| [Runs On Success](#b-runscript-runsonsuccess) | yes\|no | `yes` |  | Run the script after a successful job. |
| [Runs On Failure](#b-runscript-runsonfailure) | yes\|no | `no` |  | Run the script after a failed job as well, for example to clean up. |
| [Fail Job On Error](#b-runscript-failjobonerror) | yes\|no | `yes` |  | A script that exits with an error fails the job (for Before scripts: the job does not run). |

### Command {#b-runscript-command}

Key: `command` · Type: string

Shell command to run; repeatable. Job variables are replaced: %c client, %d Director, %e exit status, %i JobId, %j unique job name, %l level, %n job name, %s since time, %t job type, %v volume names.

```text
Command = "/usr/local/bin/dump-database %l"
```

### Console {#b-runscript-console}

Key: `console` · Type: string

Console command the Director runs instead of a shell command, for example to start another job or update a volume.

```text
Console = "update stats days=30"
```

### Runs When {#b-runscript-runswhen}

Key: `runswhen` · Type: enum · Default: `Never` · Values: `Before`, `After`, `AfterVSS`, `Always`, `Queued`

When the script runs: Before the job, After it, AfterVSS (Windows, after the snapshot), Always (before and after) or Queued (when the job enters the queue).

```text
Runs When = Before
```

### Runs On Client {#b-runscript-runsonclient}

Key: `runsonclient` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Run the command on the client (by the File Daemon) instead of on the Director.

```text
Runs On Client = no
```

### Runs On Success {#b-runscript-runsonsuccess}

Key: `runsonsuccess` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Run the script after a successful job.

```text
Runs On Success = yes
```

### Runs On Failure {#b-runscript-runsonfailure}

Key: `runsonfailure` · Type: yes|no · Default: `no` · Values: `yes`, `no`

Run the script after a failed job as well, for example to clean up.

```text
Runs On Failure = yes
```

### Fail Job On Error {#b-runscript-failjobonerror}

Key: `failjobonerror` · Type: yes|no · Default: `yes` · Values: `yes`, `no`

A script that exits with an error fails the job (for Before scripts: the job does not run).

```text
Fail Job On Error = no
```

See also: [configuration reference](../), [`configure`](/docs/commands/configure/), [`show`](/docs/commands/show/)
